attributes.body:
The adverb ほとんど is used in many situations in Japanese, and often translates as 'most', 'hardly any', 'almost all', and similar expressions. The nuance will always depend on the rest of the sentence. The most accurate translation for the word ほとんど itself is simply 'almost', where the thing that it is describing is always considered to be a full group, rather than a single thing.

As with many other adverbs that highlight an 'amount' in Japanese, ほとんど can modify a whole phrase, or can be used before の, to further specify a single noun.

In negative sentences, ほとんど translates as 'hardly any'. This is mainly due to the 'full group' that ほとんど is describing being highlighted as almost 'not' existing.

attributes.description: ほとんど definitions and example sentences

attributes.body: めったに〜ない and ほとんど can be used similarly, but with key differences. めったに〜ない means 'rarely', much like ほとんど with a negative verb. For example, めったに行かない ('I rarely go.') and ほとんど行かない ('I almost never go.') are close, though めったに suggests even lower frequency. Unlike めったに, ほとんど can also be positive, as in ほとんどみんな 'almost everyone'

second_relatable.title: ほとんど
second_relatable.meaning: Almost all, Most, Hardly any, Few (Adverbial noun)

attributes.body: Both だいたい and ほとんど can express 'most' or 'almost all,' but they also have distinct uses. For example, だいたいの人 and ほとんどの人 both mean 'most people', and だいたい一緒 and ほとんど一緒 both mean 'almost the same'. However, they diverge when ほとんど is used negatively as in ほとんどない 'almost none', as well as when だいたい means 'generally' or 'approximately' (だいたい５時に起きる), as ほとんど cannot be used here.
